match.reason: The closest bank point, Finding a rule from a graph, is about reading turning points and sine features to build a rule, and it includes sine waves that are beyond VCE Units 1 and 2 Methods, so it does not teach the idea that a parameter such as a describes a whole family of graphs.

draft.title: Families of functions
card: A parameter is a letter in a rule that can take many values. In y = ax², each value of a gives a different parabola, and together they form a family.
If a > 0 the parabola opens up. If a < 0 it opens down. The larger the size of a, the narrower the parabola.
To find the rule for one member of the family, put a given point into the rule and solve for the parameter.
Example: y = ax² passes through (2, 12). Then 12 = a × 2², so 12 = 4a and a = 3. The rule is y = 3x².
draft.remember: A parameter names a family. A point on the graph fixes which member it is.

a.q: The graph of y = ax² passes through (3, 18). What is the value of a?
a.why: Put in x = 3 and y = 18: 18 = a × 3², so 18 = 9a and a = 2. Using 3 instead of 3² gives 6, which is the tempting mistake.

b.q: The graph of y = ax² + 1 passes through (2, −7). What is its rule?
b.why: Put in the point: −7 = 4a + 1, so 4a = −8 and a = −2. Adding 1 instead of subtracting it gives 4a = −6, so −1.5, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Subtract the constant from both sides before dividing.

final.title: Families of functions
card: A parameter is a letter in a rule that can take many values. In \(y = ax^{2}\), each value of \(a\) gives a different parabola, and together they form a family.
If \(a > 0\) the parabola is concave up. If \(a < 0\) it is concave down. The larger the size of \(a\), the narrower the parabola.
To find the rule for one member of the family, put a given point into the rule and solve for the parameter.
Example: \(y = ax^{2}\) passes through \((2, 12)\). Then \(12 = a \times 2^{2}\), so \(12 = 4a\) and \(a = 3\). The rule is \(y = 3x^{2}\).

2.alt: Three members of the family \(y = ax^{2}\). With \(a = 3\) the parabola is concave up and narrow. With \(a = 1\) it is concave up and wider. With \(a = -1\) it is concave down. All three have their vertex at the origin.

final.remember: A parameter names a family. A point on the graph fixes which member it is.

a.q: The graph of \(y = ax^{2}\) passes through \((3, 18)\). What is the value of \(a\)?
a.why: Put in \(x = 3\) and \(y = 18\): \(18 = a \times 3^{2}\), so \(18 = 9a\) and \(a = 2\). Using 3 instead of \(3^{2}\) gives 6, which is the tempting mistake.

b.q: The graph of \(y = ax^{2} + 1\) passes through \((2, -7)\). What is its rule?
b.why: Put in the point: \(-7 = 4a + 1\), so \(4a = -8\) and \(a = -2\). Adding 1 instead of subtracting it gives \(4a = -6\), so \(-1.5\), which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Subtract the constant from both sides before dividing.
